problems.source_says: c117 thanks colleagues for feedback on previous versions and AOM presentations (p. 13). Candidate c917 (Sorin and Pagani, Academy of Management Proceedings 2022, DOI 10.5465/ambpp.2022.12146abstract, OpenAlex date 6 July 2022, before ChatGPT) is in this screening and queued for full text (triage path experiment_full). Its abstract says the framework 'is tested experimentally with 90 participants' generating new venture ideas, and that AI use raised cognitive flexibility and the number of creative, novel and useful ideas but lowered average novelty. Study 1 matches on authors, task, timing, analyzed N (90) and direction (Appendix D, p. 18: novelty 3.90 vs 3.97, ideas 2.71 vs 1.91). S1 and c917 very likely share one sample and need one sample_id, or at least an open question that names c917.

confirmed: Study 1 randomized 93 people: 46 to the LLM-ideas arm and 47 to the no-AI arm (p. 6, Section 4.1).
Study 1 analyzed 90 people, 45 per arm, after excluding 3 who did not complete the experiment (p. 6, Section 4.1; p. 8, Section 4.6; p. 9, Table 4).
Study 2 randomized 120 people, 60 per arm (p. 9, Section 5.1).
Study 2 analyzed 117 people, 59 in the LLM arm and 58 in the no-AI arm, after excluding 3 participants and 5 ideas as unrelated to the task (p. 9, Sections 5.1 and 5.5; p. 11, Table 6).
The paper never prints the per-arm split of exclusions. Subtraction gives 1 from the AI arm and 2 from the control arm in each study, and the form labels this as implied (p. 6; p. 8; p. 9).

All study and arm counts are people. Tables 4 and 6 are participant-level, Appendix D averages idea scores within each participant (N 45/45 and 59/58), and Table 7 counts ideas but keeps one first idea per participant (p. 8, Section 4.6.2; p. 11, Table 7; p. 18, Appendix D).
Idea totals agree with the people counts: 2.71 x 45 + 1.91 x 45 is about 208 ideas and 1.61 x 59 + 1.52 x 58 is about 183 ideas, as printed (p. 8, Section 4.6; p. 9, Section 5.5; p. 18, Appendix D).

Study 1 and Study 2 use different people: international master's students (91 percent took it in French) versus Prolific UK panel members engaged in entrepreneurship, average age about 43 (p. 6, Section 4.1; p. 9, Section 5.1).
Pretest participants are outside the counts. The paper says the first 10 were not in the final study and does not say so for the next 16 (p. 7, Section 4.3).

AI-arm participants who did not confirm the AI source (78 and 92 percent did) stay in the main analysis, and the paper says dropping them leaves results unchanged (p. 7, Section 4.3; p. 9, Section 5.3).
Each study alone has more than 50 people analyzed (90 and 117), so criterion 2 holds even if Study 1 is shared with c917 (p. 8, Section 4.6; p. 9, Section 5.5).
summary: The form's participant counts are right and printed in the paper: Study 1 randomized 93 (46/47) and analyzed 90 (45/45), Study 2 randomized 120 (60/60) and analyzed 117 (59/58), all people, so each study alone clears 50. The coding is refuted on sample overlap only: the form records no shared sample, but candidate c917 (Sorin and Pagani, AOM Proceedings 2022) reports a 90-participant new venture idea experiment that matches Study 1, so the two very likely share one sample.
